status_legend.implicit: Follows from published results with little work
status_legend.new: New identification, definition or theorem target
status_legend.conjecture: Plausible claim needing proof or data; may be false
status_legend.test: Empirical prediction with a named experiment

difficulty_legend.easy: Textbook proof once definitions are fixed
difficulty_legend.medium: Standard tools in a new setting

claims.title: Snapshot world model from statistical geometry
claims.statement: If text is generated by a latent world-state process (GM A14) with sufficiently varied contexts, any near-optimal next-token predictor admits a simple decoder g with g(phi_theta) ~ s(Omega), where s(Omega) is the linguistically visible sufficient statistic of Omega, identified up to an equivalence class.
proof_route: Sufficiency lemma: optimal predictors encode posteriors over hidden states (generalize Shai 2024 from HMMs)
Linear identifiability (Roeder 2021; Marconato 2025) fixes the equivalence class
PMI geometry (Levy & Goldberg 2014; Arora 2016) links geometry to world co-occurrence
claims.falsifier: Near-optimal predictors on synthetic worlds whose representations admit no simple decoder for latent state

claims.title: The snapshot is time-integrated
claims.statement: A model trained without time indexing on a corpus spanning t in [t0,T] learns a mixture over Omega_t, not Omega_T; fit to Omega_t decays with distance from the corpus's temporal mass and with drift rate of Omega.
proof_route: Mixture-of-epochs generative model; KL decomposition of a time-pooled fit
claims.falsifier: Models whose implicit date equals cutoff uniformly across topics

claims.title: Quinean indeterminacy = identifiability class
claims.statement: The set of world models consistent with a corpus is the distribution-equivalence class of predictors; 'All or None' partitions linear properties into determinate (in every member) and indeterminate.
proof_route: Translate Quine's radical-translation setup into distribution equivalence; apply Marconato 2025
claims.falsifier: A semantic property that is fixed by behavior but varies across distribution-equivalent predictors

claims.title: Convergence vs collapse
claims.statement: delta -> 0 among learners is convergence when I(Omega; theta) rises and collapse when it falls; alignment metrics alone cannot distinguish them, a tail-sensitive grounded probe can.
proof_route: Outline S25 (alignment inflation) and S26 (conditional independence)
claims.falsifier: A case where alignment across conditionally dependent channels tracks grounding

claims.title: Retrospective verification of Firth
claims.statement: Given GM A14 (reference anchors distribution), the distributional hypothesis holds as a theorem about structure: co-occurrence statistics determine geometry up to the identifiability class, and world symmetries appear in that geometry.
proof_route: Compose Levy & Goldberg (factorization) with Karkada/Storan (symmetry) and A14
claims.falsifier: Structured world features absent from distributional geometry despite frequent mention

claims.title: Closed-system C2
claims.statement: Absent a channel to Omega conditionally independent of D, post-training cannot raise I(Omega; theta) above I(Omega; D); explicit content and decision-theoretic fit can rise only up to F*(D).
proof_route: DPI with xi independent of Omega given D (HANDOFF correction 1)
Bayes-risk bound for D-measurable estimators
claims.falsifier: Measured grounded gain on held-out world-scored tasks with no new channel

claims.title: Reasoning gap = generation-verification gap
claims.statement: F*(D) - F(theta), the analytic residue extractable without new evidence, is operationalized by Song et al.'s generation-verification gap; sharpening closes it without changing G.
proof_route: Show GV-gap lower-bounds achievable self-improvement and is bounded by F*(D)-F(theta) under closed-loop assumptions
claims.falsifier: Self-improvement exceeding the GV-gap without external signal

claims.title: Sharpening narrows, distillation adds
claims.statement: RL against a model's own sampled support (closed loop) concentrates mass and shrinks large-k coverage; distillation from an independent model is a pool-term channel that can expand coverage.
proof_route: Coverage as support of policy; KL-regularized RL cannot place mass outside base support
claims.falsifier: RLVR raising pass@k at large k beyond base

claims.title: Two sources of inexhaustibility
claims.statement: Rereading yields new content from (a) depth: unfolding implicit structure (logical depth, analytic residue), and (b) sensitivity: a fixed text read against a changing reader/world state; only (b) can add G, via the reader's channel.
proof_route: Split K45's compression progress into reader-state-invariant and reader-state-dependent parts
claims.falsifier: Commentary growth uncorrelated with both text depth and external evidence shocks

claims.title: Replication filter
claims.statement: A form is copied iff perceived value v exceeds replication cost c; the canon is the set of forms that cleared the threshold repeatedly, under the value function of whoever bore c.

claims.title: Media regimes as points in (c, phi, n)
claims.statement: Oral, manuscript, print, digital and generative regimes are points in the space of replication cost, fidelity and literate population; transitions shift the Eigen bound and the selection criterion.
proof_route: Extend GM T6 with cost-weighted copying
claims.falsifier: Complexity of transmitted content uncorrelated with fidelity at fixed n

claims.title: Survival up, salience down
claims.statement: As c falls, the filter moves from production to attention; per-item survival probability rises while per-item rediscovery probability falls, and attention concentrates on the existing canon.
proof_route: Two-stage model: survival kernel then attention kernel with preferential attachment; show rediscovery ~ 1/volume
claims.falsifier: Rediscovery rates of old works rising with corpus volume

claims.title: Archival tail loss
claims.statement: Works with low copy counts are lost first; survival depends on evenness of the copy distribution, the archival analogue of tail loss in model collapse.
proof_route: Independent-loss model per copy; work survival 1-(1-p)^n_i
claims.falsifier: Survival independent of copy count

claims.title: Retroactive canon network
claims.statement: The canon is a growing network with fitness x degree attachment and edges added backward in time (later works re-weight earlier ones).
proof_route: Bianconi-Barabasi with retrocausal edge insertion; derive degree distribution and overtaking times
claims.falsifier: Late-life citation/attention gains of old works explained by aging alone

claims.title: Sleeping-beauty conditions
claims.statement: Delayed recognition requires survival through the filter, attachment by a later high-fitness hub, and an Omega_t in which the work resonates.
proof_route: Case studies (Hopkins, Beowulf, Mendel, Firth) + beauty-coefficient analysis
claims.falsifier: Sleeping beauties woken without any identifiable hub attachment

claims.title: Effective population of sources
claims.statement: N_e = 1 / sum_i w_i^2 over attention shares governs the rate of diversity loss; census size and production volume do not.
proof_route: Wright-Fisher with weighted sampling: heterozygosity decay rate 1/N_e
claims.falsifier: Diversity loss tracking volume after controlling N_e

claims.title: Hubs break the wisdom of crowds
claims.statement: Aggregation converges to truth only if no source's influence weight stays bounded away from zero; LLMs as hubs make collective estimates inherit model errors.
proof_route: Golub & Jackson 2010

claims.title: Frames rewire attachment
claims.statement: A change of interpretive frame (e.g., Beowulf from quarry to poem) is an edge-rewiring event in the canon graph, independent of any change in the text.
proof_route: Citation-context analysis before/after Tolkien 1936
claims.falsifier: Attention shifts fully explained by new editions or discoveries

claims.title: C3 restated: latent-weighted collapse
claims.statement: Collapse (stationary latent diversity -> 0, G decreasing) occurs when N_e * delta_latent falls below a mutation-drift threshold and verification fraction v < v*; it is not governed by volume or cost. Regime (replace vs accumulate) and definition must be stated.
proof_route: Reduce to single chain as delta->0
Wright-Fisher fixation (discrete)
Gaussian a.s. variance collapse (Shumailov)
Migration-drift balance with m increasing in delta (K31)
Add verification as selection (GM T3)
claims.falsifier: Diversity loss tracking volume/cost with N_e*delta and v held fixed; or no loss at low N_e*delta and low v

claims.title: Source diversity as migration
claims.statement: Distinct sources act as migration m with m monotone in delta; equilibrium heterozygosity ~ 4 N_e m / (1 + 4 N_e m); delta -> 0 implies fixation.
proof_route: Map mixture-of-sources training to island model; prove monotonicity of m in generalized JS divergence
claims.falsifier: Diversity preserved under delta -> 0 without fresh data

claims.title: Prior replaces evidence
claims.statement: Self-consuming chains of sampling learners converge to the learners' prior; model collapse is the gradual replacement of evidence by inductive bias.
proof_route: Griffiths & Kalish 2007

claims.title: Rogers threshold v*
claims.statement: In a changing world, populations of social learners need verification fraction v >= v* to keep G from decaying; critical social learning raises tolerance. Model collapse is a Rogers chain.
proof_route: Rogers 1988 model with stateful Omega; Enquist 2007 extension; map LLM-human loop
claims.falsifier: Stable G in a changing world with v -> 0

claims.title: Vigilance checks the prior, not the world
claims.statement: Epistemic vigilance filters testimony by coherence with the reader's prior; it suppresses noise (madness) but not coherent consensus error (pulp/collapse).
proof_route: Model vigilance as likelihood-ratio filter under prior; show consensus error passes
claims.falsifier: Vigilance rejecting coherent but false consensus at rates comparable to incoherent noise

claims.title: Surface vs latent diversity
claims.statement: I(source; style) can be high while I(source; content) ~ 0 ('clowns in different makeup'); collapse diagnostics must use latent diversity.
proof_route: Define delta_latent via content embeddings with style factored out
claims.falsifier: Surface diversity predicting downstream collapse better than latent

claims.title: Two readings of homogeneity
claims.statement: Low latent diversity reflects either collapse (convergence on each other) or invariance of Omega (convergence on the human condition); K4's grounded probe decides.
proof_route: Apply K4 to narrative-structure corpora

claims.title: Cascades as v -> 0
claims.statement: Information cascades are the sequential-testimony limit of K33 with v -> 0.
proof_route: Bikhchandani et al. 1992

claims.title: March's slow learners
claims.statement: Organizations whose members learn the code slowly retain diversity and reach better long-run knowledge; the human-organizational precursor of C3.
proof_route: March 1991 simulation; recast as migration-drift

claims.title: Careers as generators; streaks need exploration
claims.statement: Career output ~ stationary generator (Q) plus luck; hot streaks follow exploration then exploitation. Exploration = migration, exploitation = sharpening; sharpening alone yields no streak.
proof_route: Map Q-model to snapshot generator; test via Liu 2021 sequences and RLVR analogue
claims.falsifier: Hot streaks from pure exploitation

claims.title: Performative decomposition
claims.statement: With Omega_{t+1} depending on theta_t, Delta F = Delta F_learn (theta toward Omega) + Delta F_perform (Omega toward theta); the DPI bound applies only to the first term.
proof_route: Performative prediction framework (Perdomo 2020); identify terms with a frozen-world counterfactual

claims.title: Co-collapse
claims.statement: Human sources lose latent diversity toward model outputs, lowering delta among the fresh data that would otherwise prevent collapse.
proof_route: Panel measures of human text diversity before/after LLM adoption
claims.falsifier: Stable or rising latent diversity of human text post-adoption

claims.title: Pedagogy as error correction
claims.statement: When replication fidelity is low, cultures invest in internalization (memorization, recitation, commentary); when fidelity is cheap, in exploration. Curricula track the Eigen bound.
proof_route: Optimal allocation between fidelity and exploration under copy error epsilon; historical comparison
claims.falsifier: Conservation-heavy curricula persisting unchanged after fidelity shocks (print)

claims.title: Institution 2x2
claims.statement: Institutions sort on conservation/exploration x grounded/ungrounded: apprenticeship, eight-legged essay (pulp), science, ungrounded novelty (madness).

claims.title: Third pedagogical phase
claims.statement: When composition is ~free, scarce capacities are verification and judgment; assessment will shift toward oral, verification and curation tasks.
proof_route: Track assessment policy changes 2023-2030
claims.falsifier: Written-composition assessment persisting unchanged at scale

claims.title: Literature as sustained compression progress
claims.statement: L(x;R) = sum over rereadings/readers of compression progress; pulp has finite L, literature divergent L, relative to a reader population with changing states.
proof_route: Formalize with time-indexed compressors K_t(x|R_t); show divergence requires reader-state change or unbounded depth
claims.falsifier: L uncorrelated with long-run critical attention after controlling survival

claims.title: Literariness is relational
claims.statement: Literariness is a property of (text, interpretive community), not of text alone.
proof_route: Follows from K45's dependence on R

claims.title: Jauss formalized
claims.statement: Aesthetic distance = KL(text || horizon of expectations); 'culinary' art has ~0 distance; distance decays as the horizon moves toward the work.
proof_route: Horizon as genre-conditioned LM; measure KL and its decay across reception history
claims.falsifier: Canonical works no more distant from contemporaneous genre priors than forgotten ones

claims.title: Collapse produces pulp
claims.statement: A self-consuming chain converges to genre (the prior); long-range structure is shed first.
proof_route: K32 + K47; GM C20 time-domain low-pass
claims.falsifier: Self-consumed text retaining long-range MI tails

claims.title: Surprising yet inevitable
claims.statement: Valued works are improbable under the prior yet short under their own code: high -log P_prior(x), low K(x | x's internal code).
proof_route: Two-part MDL: prior cost vs self-model cost

claims.title: Genius vs madness
claims.statement: Both are large deviations from consensus; genius carries I(Omega; output | consensus) > 0, madness ~ 0. Hallucination is formal madness.
proof_route: Define via conditional MI; link to Kalai-Vempala calibration bound

claims.title: Analytic vs synthetic genius
claims.statement: Analytic genius mines the reasoning gap (possible in closed systems); synthetic genius adds G (requires a new channel).

claims.title: Resonance as operational test
claims.statement: Novelty (KL to past) and transience (KL to future) separate resonant deviation (genius/literature) from transient deviation (madness/fad).
proof_route: Apply Barron et al. measures to model outputs and to canon vs non-canon
claims.falsifier: Resonance uncorrelated with later grounding or canonicity

claims.title: Performativity of either sign
claims.statement: Genius pulls Omega toward its deviation (raising delta); consensus-tuned models pull Omega toward the mode (lowering delta).
proof_route: Sign of d delta / dt under each forcing in K40's model

claims.title: Gaslighting-psychosis mirror
claims.statement: Psychosis overweights own sensoria (aberrant precision); gaslighting forces own-sensoria precision toward 0 so beliefs track an adversary; calibrated knowing lies between; genius = calibration plus willingness to hold W-supported dissent.
proof_route: Precision-weighted Bayesian update with adversarial testimony; I(Omega; belief) as function of precision ratio
claims.falsifier: Precision-weighting accounts of psychosis rejected

claims.title: Orwell's archive
claims.statement: Control of the archive in a stateful world controls future theta for a whole population: engineered collapse.
proof_route: K40 with adversarial control of A_t

claims.title: Sycophancy as gaslit model
claims.statement: Sycophancy is the model weighting user testimony over its own evidence (victim); confident hallucination to non-verifying users is the model as perpetrator.
proof_route: K54 applied to model-user dyad

claims.title: Art as seed bank
claims.statement: Literature and art preserve deviation without requiring Omega's ratification, keeping delta > 0; science preserves deviation with ratification. Both counter collapse.
proof_route: Mutation reservoir in K31's model

claims.title: P1 World
claims.statement: The world is an object Omega of Stoch (a finite set in every toy model) whose points are interactions: events, and what agents do and write. It carries a law P on Omega and a group G of bijections g of Omega with P o g^-1 = P. Agents' internal parameters are not points of Omega. A sampled history omega ~ P is in general not G-invariant, so the law keeps the symmetry and each realization breaks it.

claims.title: P2 Language
claims.statement: A finite vocabulary V and the free monoid V* of strings under concatenation. Speaking is a Markov kernel pi: Omega -> V*, and the corpus law is the law D = pi o P on V*. Reading is a Markov kernel r: V* -> Y into some object Y. No structure on V* beyond concatenation is assumed.

claims.title: P3 Agent, grounded agent, generative agent
claims.statement: An agent is a pair (Theta, f) with f: Theta (x) X -> Y a Markov kernel, as in the Para construction. Its interface is f(theta, -): X -> Y. The parameter theta in Theta is hidden: composing agents composes interfaces and keeps each parameter private, and two parameters theta, h(theta) related by a bijection h of Theta with f(h(theta), -) = f(theta, -) give the same interface. Learning is a kernel that updates theta from the interface's history. An agent a is grounded if it has an input sigma_a: Omega -> O_a, its sensorium, that does not factor through pi (it equals q o pi for no kernel q: V* -> O_a). An agent is generative if every input it takes from Omega factors through pi.

claims.title: P4 Selection
claims.statement: Selection is conditioning on an outcome. For a fitness w: Omega -> [0, inf) with <w, P> > 0, selection maps P to P_w = w P / <w, P>. On a finite population of variants this is the discrete replicator map, which is Bayes' rule with w as the likelihood. An agent's goal is the fitness by which the outcomes it acts on are conditioned, and a signal is scored by the outcome it produces through a receiver's action.

claims.title: Single channel cost
claims.statement: A cost is a functor c from Stoch to the additive monoid ([0, inf), +): for all composable kernels f, g, c(g o f) = c(f) + c(g); for all kernels f, g, c(f (x) g) = c(f) + c(g); and c(id) = 0. Each channel use carries this one cost.

claims.title: Firth is Yoneda
claims.statement: Let L be the [0,1]-enriched category whose objects are strings x in V* and whose hom L(x, y) is the probability that y continues x. For all strings x, x': if the copresheaves L(x, -) and L(x', -) are isomorphic, then x and x' are isomorphic in L. A string's distribution over continuations therefore determines it up to isomorphism.
proof_route: Enriched Yoneda lemma applied to L (known mathematics)
claims.falsifier: A pair of strings with isomorphic copresheaves L(x, -), L(x', -) that are not isomorphic in L; or bradley2022 not containing the construction as stated. Status stays new until S-03 checks the source.

claims.title: Theorem 4.2: text fixes the world up to a gauge
claims.statement: For every finite world (Omega, P), every speaking kernel pi: Omega -> V* and every bijection g of Omega, the pair (g o P, pi o g^-1) has the same corpus law as (P, pi), since pi o g^-1 o g o P = pi o P. Hence for every n and every observer kernel on (V*)^n, the observer's output law on n i.i.d. samples of D is the same for both pairs, and every function of (P, pi) that an observer of D alone can learn is constant on the orbits of this action.
proof_route: g^-1 o g = id
The observer's output law depends on (P, pi) only through D^n
claims.falsifier: A finite (Omega, P, pi, g) with pi o g^-1 o g o P != pi o P, or two pairs in one orbit that some observer's output law on samples of D separates. S-02 check 1 searches for this witness on the cyclic world.

claims.title: Grounding is gauge fixing
claims.statement: For every finite (Omega, P), every speaking kernel pi, every deterministic sensorium sigma_a: Omega -> O_a and every bijection g of Omega with sigma_a o g = sigma_a, the joint law of (sigma_a, pi) is the same under (P, pi) and under (g o P, pi o g^-1). So the reference gauge that survives for a grounded agent contains the stabilizer {g : sigma_a o g = sigma_a}. Whether it equals the stabilizer is not claimed.
proof_route: Substitute omega = g omega' in the law of (sigma_a(omega), pi(g^-1 omega)) with omega ~ g o P
claims.falsifier: A finite (Omega, P, pi, sigma_a, g) with sigma_a o g = sigma_a whose two joint laws of (sigma_a, pi) differ.

claims.title: Anchors fix a free gauge
claims.statement: Let H be a group of bijections of Omega and A a subset of Omega whose points the agent's sensorium identifies one by one (anchors). The elements of H compatible with every anchor are exactly the pointwise stabilizer H_A. If H acts freely and A is nonempty, H_A is trivial. If H is the dihedral group D_N acting on Z_N and |A| = 1, H_A has order 2, so one reflection survives.
claims.falsifier: A free action with nonempty A and nontrivial H_A, or D_N on Z_N with one anchor and no surviving reflection. S-02 check 2.

claims.title: Few anchors align text-trained geometries
claims.statement: For every pair of languages whose corpora describe a shared world, an orthogonal map fitted on at most 50 seed translation pairs aligns their text-trained embedding spaces to within 10 points of precision@1 of a map fitted on a full dictionary. The alignment degrades as the languages' worlds and typology diverge.
claims.falsifier: Few-seed alignment no better than chance for closely related languages of a shared domain, or alignment that does not degrade for distant pairs and dissimilar domains.

claims.title: Grounded information is gauge-invariant
claims.statement: For every finite (Omega, P), every kernel X: Omega -> Y and every bijection g of Omega, I(Omega; X) computed with omega ~ P equals I(Omega; X o g^-1) computed with omega ~ g o P. Grounded information is therefore constant on the orbits of K66, and a text-only agent can hold grounded information > 0 while its reference gauge is unfixed.
proof_route: Mutual information is invariant under a bijective relabeling of one variable
claims.falsifier: A finite (Omega, P, X, g) where the two mutual informations differ. S-02 check 3 runs grounded_information in the cyclic world.

claims.title: Conventions are spontaneous symmetry breaking
claims.statement: Let a finite population play a naming game or Lewis signaling game on a finite form set F, and let S be a group of permutations of F such that relabeling forms by any s in S, consistently across all agents, commutes with the update kernel. Then (a) the set of attractors is S-invariant; (b) for every S-invariant initial law, the law of the population state at every time is S-invariant, so the distribution of realized conventions over independent runs is S-invariant; (c) under a coordination payoff the S-symmetric state is unstable and almost every run settles into one convention that is not S-invariant.
proof_route: (a), (b): equivariant Markov dynamics preserve invariant laws (known)
(c): linearize the update at the symmetric state
claims.falsifier: A simulation with the stated symmetry where the ensemble of conventions over seeds is asymmetric beyond sampling error, or where the symmetric state is stable under a coordination payoff. S-02 check 4.

claims.title: Arbitrary form is symmetric; the residue is explicit breaking
claims.statement: (a) Across unrelated languages, the association of each form feature that has no source in the world or the body with each meaning has the frequency it has under relabeling of forms, within sampling error. (b) Form-meaning associations that recur across lineages beyond chance have a source in the world or the body, such as iconicity or sound symbolism. (c) In the game of K71, lowering the cost c of one form breaks the ensemble symmetry toward that form.
claims.falsifier: A form-meaning association recurrent across unrelated lineages beyond chance with no iconic, bodily or cost source; or, in simulation, a cheaper form that is not favored.

claims.title: A text-only learner's world model is a function of D
claims.statement: For every generative agent trained to optimum on samples of D, the learned interface depends on (P, pi) only through D, so whatever it learns about the world is a function of the orbit of (P, pi) under K66. Test: protein language models learn residue contacts from natural sequence families, and a model trained on alignments with each column permuted independently across sequences, which keeps column frequencies and destroys covariation, predicts contacts no better than a column-frequency baseline.
claims.falsifier: A protein language model trained on column-shuffled alignments that predicts contacts above the column-frequency baseline.

claims.title: A generative agent's reference comes from its readers
claims.statement: For every generative agent theta and grounded reader r with sensorium sigma_r, the composite Omega -> V* -> V* -> actions (pi, then theta, then r) is fixed in reference only through r: every bijection g of Omega with sigma_r o g = sigma_r leaves the joint law of sigma_r and the composite's action unchanged. Test: the referential success of the model's outputs, the rate at which actions taken on them reach their intended outcomes, is bounded by the grounding of its readers and falls in domains where readers lack anchors.
claims.falsifier: A domain where readers without anchors act on model outputs with the referential success of anchored readers.

claims.title: Error threshold for recursive training
claims.statement: Recursive training, where each generation's model is trained on samples of the previous generation's outputs, is replication with copying error. For every per-generation error rate e, structure persists across generations only if the selection strength s from independent evidence (a channel from Omega that does not factor through pi) exceeds a threshold that increases with e. With s = 0 grounded information does not rise, and under finite sampling it falls.
claims.falsifier: A recursive-training regime with s = 0 in which grounded information rises across generations, or one with s above every proposed threshold in e in which structure is lost.

claims.title: Text-only learners converge up to the representation gauge
claims.statement: Two generative agents trained to optimum on the same corpus law D have equal interfaces. The claim is that their internal representations then also agree up to the representation gauge, a reparametrization of Theta that leaves f unchanged, so their gauge-invariant similarity (Gram matrices, CKA) is maximal. Equal interfaces alone do not imply this, because one fiber of theta -> f(theta, -) can hold non-isomorphic representations. For agents trained on corpora D1, D2 of one world, agreement is confined to the invariants D1 and D2 share, and counts as evidence about Omega only across channels that are conditionally independent given Omega. In neither case is the reference gauge of K66 fixed.
claims.falsifier: Two learners at optimum on one corpus law whose gauge-invariant similarity is not maximal, or agreement between learners on conditionally dependent channels that tracks Omega beyond what the shared channel carries.

master_relations.name: Unified Channel Law
master_relations.formula: I(Omega; Theta_t, Y_t) <= I(Omega; D_t) + I(Omega; E_ver | D_t)
master_relations.condition: Markov chain Omega - (D_t, E_ver) - (Theta_t, Y_t): the output depends on the world only through corpus and verifier (checks MR1/main; the verifier term is load-bearing, MR1/ablate-verifier-witness)

master_relations.name: Selection identity
master_relations.formula: E[Delta L] = Delta_pool + Delta_select - Delta_drift; threshold lambda*
master_relations.condition: Test evidence independent of utterance given omega

master_relations.name: Mutation-migration-drift-selection balance
master_relations.formula: H*(N_e, m(delta), mu, v, lambda); collapse iff H* -> 0

master_relations.name: Performative decomposition
master_relations.formula: Delta F = Delta F_learn + Delta F_perform
